data.long_meaning: Derived from the Greek word 'arondios' meaning 'strong, powerful'. In ancient Greece, the name Arundel was given to warriors and those who built and defended fortresses. In Christianity, Arundel is a name for boys symbolizing strength and protection. The name Arundel carries the meaning “Powerful fortress” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Arundel usually hope their child will grow to embody powerful fortress and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A symbol of spiritual fortitude and protection.
data.etymology: Arundel belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Powerful fortress.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Arundel total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

data.spiritual_significance: In Christianity, the name Arundel symbolizes not only physical strength but also spiritual power. It is a name for boys that reflects their potential to be strong in their faith and protect their loved ones and community. Thus, those named Arundel are encouraged to live up to its meaning and be a source of strength and protection for those around them.

modern_usage.modern_context: Arundel is a surname of English origin and has been in use since the Middle Ages. It is derived from the name of the historic castle in Sussex, England, which was the seat of the Dukes of Norfolk. The name has been popular in England and has spread to other English-speaking countries due to emigration and colonialism.
